Hi all! Getting back to what started this thread off, here’s my division of Sarracenia “Black” that I was lucky enough to snag from Mike last year (same clone from Mike’s first post). It arrived bare-root in late May 2022, and by the end of August it was already wicked dark:

here it is next to HCW F just for fun:

It’s putting up a flower and pitcher right now, and you’d better believe I’m eager to see how it breeds! If the timing works out I’d love to cross it with something like Mike’s moorei “dark pink” (see below) which, based on my preliminary efforts, also seems to pass on some killer darkness to its offspring.

The goal here is to make something a little chunkier and less tall/lanky than S. “Black”, perhaps with some areolae or venation to make the appearance more complex and interesting. And hey, these dark genetics are full of surprises, so maybe I’ll get something even darker than the parents! Don’t get me wrong, S. “Black” is gorgeous already—huge props to Mike again—but I think this is just the beginning of black Sarracenia breeding and I’m stoked to see what we can do moving forward! Anybody else grow this clone? What else would you cross it with?

posts.body_html:
Mike's S. "Black" (the same clone that started this thread) is looking gnarly already. It's like an ominous looming shadow--sticks out like a sore thumb every time I check on the crops. It's not quite black in person, but it's a seriously deep purplish red, and I'm sure it'll keep coloring up as the season progresses

Here it is at dusk on May 25th:


And a couple artsy photos at sunset tonight. If you're wondering about the trippy focus, I was actually holding my lens freely in front of my camera (so-called "lens whacking") to approximate a tilt-shift lens. Fun stuff


A wider shot--can you spot "Black" on the left? Btw, here's where tilt-shifting really shines. The plants that stretch across the middle of the photo aren't all the same distance from the camera, yet they're all in focus! If you've ever seen those time-lapses of a city or construction site or something where everything looks tiny, as if it were a miniature toy or railroad set, that's the same effect at play.

posts.body_html:
Here is a population of flava var. atroprpurpurea taking color. The sun and the heat of the last few days have made up for the delay in coloring. In the foreground S. leucophylla ‘Mont Blanc’ x ‘Bocaza’


Then here is a young Sarracenia x (S. oreophila Sand Mountain X S. atropurpurea ‘Black Water’) Clone 1 which flowered this year for the 1st time: robust pitcher, large lid and very dark coloring are its assets.


Alone and in the company of a very young, from a dark lineage (F149 MK x F124MK) of which 2 - 3 individuals from the cross have very dark sought-after characters.



The flava population is grown outdoors unlike the other 2 which are grown in greenhouse. Their dark coloring is all the more interesting (outside the dark is more intense).


The F124 MK (Don Schnell) is at the bottom left, 1st row with a few yellow spots on the lid.
